content:
Unit 1 - Main Idea & Purpose — Title & Goal
Learn to master unit 1 - main idea & purpose questions for the Digital SAT through a short concept, a modeled item, and targeted practice.

Key skill

Read the note and focus on what the question is really asking inside the passage.

  • Locate explicit claims and implicit ideas.
  • Ask: What is the passage mainly doing?
  • Match answers to the most general accurate statement.

Model item

Study how the evidence in the passage supports the correct answer.

Passage — In a memo to staff, the museum director explains that extending evening hours increased visitors by 18% but strained security staffing. The memo recommends partnering with a local college to staff late shifts while maintaining the new hours.

Question 1. Which choice best states the main point of the memo?

  • The museum should reduce hours to ease staffing demands.
  • Evening hours boosted attendance; a partnership can solve staffing issues.
  • College students will volunteer at the museum on weekends only.
  • Security concerns outweigh the benefits of evening hours.
The memo highlights growth from evening hours and proposes a partnership solution, matching B.

Quick practice

Try these quickly. Eliminate two choices before choosing your answer.

Passage — The farmer describes rotating crops to restore soil nutrients and reduce pests without chemical sprays.

Question 2. Which choice best expresses the central idea?

  • Crop rotation improves soil health and pest control naturally.
  • Chemical sprays are the only way to prevent pests.
  • Rotating crops is too complex for most farms.
  • Farmers avoid changing their growing schedules.
The farmer endorses rotation as a natural method accomplishing both goals, A.

Passage — A coach argues that shorter practices with precise drills outperform longer, unfocused sessions.

Question 3. Which choice best summarizes the passage?

  • Athletes should practice less often.
  • Long practices are better for endurance.
  • Focused, shorter practices can be more effective than long, unfocused ones.
  • Coaches should cancel practices before tournaments.
The contrast favors shorter, focused sessions → C.

Next skill

Build on the previous skill. Compare how this question type reads the passage differently.

Note: Locate the exact phrase or sentence that proves your choice.

Another model item

Notice how small wording differences change the best answer.

Passage — A historian notes that while a new archive digitization is incomplete, it already allows scholars worldwide to access rare letters once limited to on-site visits.

Question 4. Which choice best captures the author’s main point?

  • Digitization is unnecessary for serious scholars.
  • Remote access is now possible even before the project is finished.
  • The archive will close until digitization is complete.
  • Only local scholars benefit from the project.
The author emphasizes new accessibility despite partial completion → B.

More practice

Aim for accuracy first, then speed. Re-check the evidence that rules out each wrong choice.

Passage — The editorial praises a city composting program that lowered landfill use and suggests expanding pickup routes.

Question 5. Which choice states the editorial’s central claim?

  • Composting failed to reduce landfill use.
  • The city should expand composting pickup routes after early success.
  • Recycling is more important than composting.
  • Residents oppose changes to waste collection.

Mixed practice set

These mix multiple skills. Mark the question type before you start, then solve.

Passage — A lab report concludes that adding insulation around water pipes reduced heat loss in winter by 35%.

Question 6. Which choice best expresses the report’s main conclusion?

  • Insulating pipes increases heat loss in summer.
  • Insulating pipes reduced winter heat loss substantially.
  • Pipe insulation is illegal in some regions.
  • Heat loss has no impact on energy bills.
